{"claims":[{"claim_text":"President Obama removed U.S. combat brigades and ended the U.S. combat mission in Iraq on a 19-month timetable after taking office.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. completed the drawdown of all U.S. troops in Iraq last December after an interim period of advising Iraqis and conducting counterterrorism operations.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The decision to complete the drawdown of U.S. troops in Iraq was reached after extensive discussions and with the full agreement of the Iraqi government.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The decision to complete the drawdown of U.S. troops in Iraq was determined to be in the best interest of both the U.S. and Iraq.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Mitt Romney and many Republicans would have preferred to leave tens of thousands of U.S. troops in Iraq in an open-ended commitment.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The preferred commitment of Mitt Romney and many Republicans was against the will of the Iraqi government and people.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"President Obama and the Democratic Party are committed to building a robust, long-term strategic partnership with a sovereign, united, and democratic Iraq in diplomatic, economic, and security fields.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The partnership with Iraq is based on mutual interests and mutual respect.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
